meta.title: Qualify path loses path segment
meta.build_notes: GitHub release assets rust-analyzer-aarch64-apple-darwin.gz of the weekly tags 2026-05-11 and 2026-05-18; git tag --contains puts the fix first in 2026-05-18. The sysroot is the local rustup toolchain (rustc 1.98.1).
meta.notes: The qualify_path assist rebuilt the path from the resolved item's module path and dropped the segment 'ext' when the cursor was on the last segment: 'make::ext::foo' became 'ast::make::foo'. Attempt 1 (diagnostics after the edit) could not see the wrong path because rust-analyzer does not report the unresolved multi-segment path; attempt 2 compares with the issue's expected text (specification probe).

settings_note: The issue names no settings; the session keeps checkOnSave off (native analysis only).

files.note: the module line verbatim; the path expression 'make::ext::foo' (cursor marker $0 removed) is placed as a statement in an added fn main, since a bare path is not an item
a binary crate around the snippet (package name, version, edition 2021)

repro.steps: Open src/main.rs. With the cursor at the end of the unresolved path 'make::ext::foo' (line 2, character 18, the issue's $0) apply the qualify-path fix (Qualify ...). Reported: 'ast::make::foo', which does not resolve; expected 'ast::make::ext::foo'. Probe (specification, attempt 2): the edited src/main.rs must equal the issue's expected result, the path qualified as ast::make::ext::foo.

expected.source: issue body ('expect' block: ast::make::ext::foo), in the same fn main

attempts.summary: Qualify-path fix checked with a fresh session on the edited text: not-reproduced-pre. The pre build 2026-05-11 did make the reported wrong edit ('ast::make::foo;', segment ext lost; the post build 2026-05-18 wrote 'ast::make::ext::foo;'), but rust-analyzer reports no diagnostic for the unresolved multi-segment path (neither before nor after the edit), so the diagnostic probe cannot see it.
